turns.prompt_text: Would any of the lights I own work with this?
turns.response_html:
Based on the lights you've mentioned and purchased recently, none of your current bulbs are a direct, safe match for that specific GE ProLine ballast ($GE260ISMV-N-DIYB$).

Here is why your existing inventory won't work with it:

The Compatibility Gap

  • The T8 and T12 LED Tubes: You have GE Universal and Great Value 4-foot LED tubes. While "Universal" LEDs are designed to work with many ballasts, that specific GE ballast is a Rapid Start model meant for 8-foot T12 lamps. Most 4-foot LED tubes are designed for "Instant Start" ballasts or direct line voltage (ballast bypass). Using them with an 8-foot ballast could overdrive the LEDs and cause them to fail or overheat.
  • The T5 Bulbs: Your 6-inch Sylvania F4T5 and the Zoo Med ReptiSun 15W HO are physically and electrically incompatible. T5s are much thinner and require significantly different voltages and pin-outs than the large T12 pins this ballast uses.
  • Physical Length: This ballast is specifically tuned for 8-foot (96-inch) lamps. Even if you had T12 bulbs, if they are only 4 feet long, the electrical load wouldn't match the ballast's output profile.

What Would Work

If you want to use this ballast, you would need to pick up:

  • Standard F96T12 fluorescent tubes (the classic 8-foot "fat" tubes).
  • 8-foot LED replacement tubes specifically rated for "Ballast Compatible" (Plug-and-Play) use with T12 Rapid Start ballasts.

My Recommendation

Since you’ve been doing quite a bit of electrical work and DIY repairs lately, you might find it easier to bypass the ballast entirely. Most of the 4-foot LED tubes you own (like the Great Value ones) often support "Type B" installation, where you remove the ballast and wire the sockets directly to your house power.

Would you like me to check the specific model numbers of your LED tubes to see if they support a "ballast bypass" installation instead?
